reasoning_traces.think:
The tendency regeneration process operates on a deterministic pipeline where play-by-play data in parquet format serves as input. Each season's data is read into a structured table with 160 offense and defense rows, ensuring symmetry and completeness. The seed row is constructed from an earlier version of the dataset, which may contain fewer weeks. As such, any subsequent refresh must generate a new vintage rather than silently replacing the existing seed. This prevents loss of historical context and maintains model stability. When comparing regenerated tendencies against committed seeds, discrepancies like those seen in 2026 CLE indicate either data drift or algorithmic variance. The system enforces consistency checks to validate that regenerated values align with expected outcomes, thereby upholding the integrity of probabilistic forecasts used in GSI’s Bayesian inference framework.
